clue.text: Method of quantifying gravel

definitions.meaning: a mathematical system for working out rates and quantities
in medicine, small stones formed in the kidney or bladder

explanation.surface: Someone asks how to measure a heap of gravel.
explanation.definitionFit: Calculus is a branch of mathematics for measuring change, and in medicine a calculus is a stone, such as the grit called gravel in the kidneys.

clue.text: No traces, possibly. of this old grandsire

indicators.note: the letters might be arranged another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: An old forefather left no traces behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandsire is a forefather, one from whom a family descends.

clue.text: Recovering to study the fragrance of the valley

indicators.note: the fragrance belongs to the valley, so the valley's word comes first

parts.note: to con is to study or learn
a vale is a valley
a scent is a pleasant smell

explanation.surface: A patient gets better studying the scent of a valley's flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Convalescent describes someone getting better after illness.

clue.text: Played by Lawrence, maybe, in flimsy clothing?

indicators.note: the name goes inside the delicate fabric

parts.note: lace is a fine open fabric
T. E. Lawrence enlisted in the RAF under the name Ross

explanation.surface: Lawrence of Arabia plays a sport dressed in delicate lace.
explanation.walkthrough: Lawrence of Arabia joined the RAF as Aircraftman Ross.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacrosse is a team sport played with netted sticks.

clue.text: Sharper's piece of equivocation, no doubt

definitions.text: Sharper's piece of equivocation, no doubt

parts.words: Sharper's piece of equivocation, no doubt
parts.note: a card cheat's move with the deck, which is also the word for evasive dodging

explanation.definitionFit: Shuffling is mixing cards, which a cheat exploits, and also evasive, shifty talk.

clue.text: A degree for Gail, we hear, lucky thing!

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts
the name Gail sounds like Gael, and a Gael is a Scot

explanation.surface: Gail earns a degree and calls it her good-luck charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns Gail into Gael, a Highland Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: A mascot is a charm or figure believed to bring good fortune.

clue.text: But he doesn't fly from Waikiki willingly

indicators.note: the letters are taken from inside the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A man happily refuses to leave Waikiki by plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi is New Zealand's flightless bird.

clue.text: Bleep a number all over the place for the tall thin chap

indicators.note: scattered in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pager sends out a scattered number to a lanky fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanpole is slang for a tall skinny person, after the stake used for climbing beans.

clue.text: Command a military formation prominent in the press

parts.note: to head is to lead or command
troops drawn up side by side form a line

explanation.surface: An officer orders troops into formation, and it makes the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A banner title in large type is the most prominent text on a newspaper page.

clue.text: Fashionable surround for colonel's statue

indicators.note: the word for fashionable is placed around the letters standing for the colonel

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
CO, commanding officer, is the post a colonel holds

explanation.surface: A trendy setting is chosen for a statue of the colonel.
explanation.definitionFit: An icon is a sacred image or likeness, so a carved figure or statue qualifies.

clue.text: Old, true-sounding stories about a confirmation

indicators.note: the old word for true is heard, and its spelling is taken from that sound

parts.note: very once meant true or genuine, as in 'very God of very God'

indicators.note: the word for stories goes round the single letter supplied by 'a'

parts.note: fiction means invented stories

explanation.surface: An old tale that only rings true is said to confirm something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old, true' points to the archaic adjective once meaning genuine, as in 'very God of very God'; 'sounding' keeps only its sound, spelt with a final I. 'about' wraps the stories round A.
explanation.definitionFit: Verification is the act of checking that something is so, which is a confirmation.

clue.text: Law-breaker upset strangers? So right

indicators.note: turned over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Strangers are upset by an offender; so be it.
explanation.definitionFit: A transgressor is one who breaks a rule or law.

clue.text: Poles on foot engage in contest on board

indicators.note: the contest is engaged inside the letters for being on board ship

parts.note: SS, steamship, is the crossword convention for aboard a vessel
a tilt is a joust, a contest on horseback

explanation.surface: Sailors are told to take up a joust on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilts are long poles with footrests, used for walking raised above the ground.

clue.text: Libertine unwilling to have a large port

parts.note: loth means reluctant or unwilling
Rio de Janeiro, the great Brazilian harbour city

explanation.surface: A rake is reluctant to drink a big glass of port wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' suggests the drink, but it is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: A Lothario is a seducer, after the rake in Rowe's play The Fair Penitent.

clue.text: Harassed newspaperman forcibly enlisted

definitions.meaning: taken into the navy by a press gang

explanation.surface: A reporter, pestered, finds himself press-ganged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newspaperman' is a nod to the press and its editor (ED), joining the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard pressed means harassed, and pressed men were sailors seized by the press gang.

clue.text: He may talk down through being out of reach

indicators.note: the word for through sits outside the other word

parts.note: per means by way of or through
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man shouts down from somewhere nobody can get at him.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher addresses the congregation from the raised pulpit, lecturing listeners.

clue.text: Spend a long time on the journey

parts.note: to pass time is to spend it
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone spends ages travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A passage is a voyage, especially a crossing by sea.

clue.text: Where we may be landed to publicize wines

parts.note: to air a view is to make it public
ports are fortified wines

explanation.surface: Advertising wines at the place where we arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: Airports are where aircraft set passengers down.

clue.text: Food substance or horse in ancient language? Quite the opposite

indicators.note: the clue says horse goes into the language
reverses that instruction, so the language goes into the horse

parts.note: gee, or gee-gee, is a child's word for a horse
Latin, the language of ancient Rome

explanation.surface: Is this food made from horse, or is it ancient Latin?
explanation.definitionFit: Gelatine is a protein used to set jellies and other foods.

clue.text: Reminder of fellows in New York Opera's "Ring"

indicators.note: the men go inside the opera house's name

parts.note: the Met, New York's Metropolitan Opera
men are fellows
O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: Wagner's Ring at the Met leaves a keepsake of the men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' tempts as Wagner's cycle; here it is just O.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a keepsake, kept to recall something.

clue.text: Noted precision of supporting actors

definitions.meaning: accuracy in playing written notes together
a company of players working as a group

explanation.surface: Musicians playing exactly together are praised, along with the backing cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Players keeping exact time together show good ensemble, and a cast working as a group is an ensemble.

clue.text: One who scarpers from a shelter?

definitions.meaning: someone who runs away; to do a bunk is British slang for fleeing

explanation.surface: Someone flees from a refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to do a bunk is to run off, so a bunker flees; a bunker is also a fortified shelter.

clue.text: It's not often gunners display trust

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery
to rely on someone is to trust them

explanation.surface: Artillerymen seldom show faith in anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means seldom or infrequently.

clue.text: Quarrelsome old union leaders in various vessels

parts.note: a can and some tankers are vessels of different kinds

indicators.note: the leading letters go inside the second of the vessels

parts.note: a can and some tankers are vessels of different kinds

indicators.note: the first letters of the words old and union

explanation.surface: Grumpy veteran trade union bosses are scattered across several ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantankerous means bad-tempered and argumentative.

clue.text: Japanese drama satisfactory for the recess

parts.note: No, or Noh, is classical Japanese masked theatre
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A Japanese play is fine for the school break.
explanation.definitionFit: A nook is a small recess or corner.

clue.text: Begin a voyage in Greater Manchester, say?

indicators.note: the town's name is spoken, and the spelling comes from what is heard

parts.note: Sale is a town in Greater Manchester, England

explanation.surface: Someone sets off on a trip from the Manchester area.
explanation.walkthrough: SALE is a town in Greater Manchester; said out loud it matches the word for setting off by boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To sail is to set out on a sea trip.

clue.text: Quote Lenin wrongly? Not in speaking persuasively

indicators.note: quoting incorrectly jumbles the letters of the two words
the two letters of the word in are left out of the scrambled pool

explanation.surface: Misquoting Lenin is no way to make a convincing speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrongly' scrambles QUOTELENIN; 'Not in' removes I and N.
explanation.definitionFit: An eloquent person is fluent and forceful in speech.

clue.text: Alumnus as acolyte, keeping an eye on things

parts.note: OB, old boy, a former pupil
an altar server assists the priest

explanation.surface: A former pupil serving at the altar keeps watch.
explanation.definitionFit: An observer is one who watches, someone keeping a look-out.
